brief.title: JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive overview of the official JavaScript web framework benchmark spanning Chrome 55 through Chrome 146, tracking how the testing methodology and ecosystem have evolved.
brief.goal: Viewers should understand the scale, longevity, and methodology of the JS Framework Benchmark, appreciate key milestones in its evolution, and recognize why cross-version comparisons require caution.

sections.title: What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?
sections.objective: Introduce the benchmark's purpose: comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations in Chrome, and explain why it matters to the developer community.

sections.title: Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146
sections.objective: Visualize the history of 60+ official benchmark runs across 8 years (2017–2026), highlighting platform coverage (OSX vs Windows) and keyed-only vs full runs.

sections.title: Methodology Milestones
sections.objective: Highlight the key methodology changes — the switch to weighted geometric mean in Chrome 118, CPU throttling adjustments, and measurement fine-tuning — and why cross-version comparisons are unsafe.

sections.title: Platform & Framework Coverage at a Glance
sections.objective: Show the breakdown of runs by year and platform, and note the alternating pattern of keyed-only vs full framework runs in recent versions.

sections.title: Key Takeaways for Developers
sections.objective: Summarize actionable insights: always compare within the same Chrome version, consult the latest run for current standings, and understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.
